summary:
SL-009 does what PS-017 and the merged SC-018 ask, and nothing I ran contradicts the build. I checked it against the code, not a live deployment.

**What I ran** (TAAD3_HOME set to an empty scratch folder each time):
- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `go test -count=1 ./...` passes in all 11 packages.
- The architecture rules all hold (29 of 29).
- E-005's finish test exits 0: "Ran 1 test … OK" in 4.5 s. I read its body from the ledger in place (mode=ro, `SELECT finish FROM epics WHERE id=43`) and ran a scratch copy with ROOT patched to this worktree. It builds `./cmd/hband` and serves it against the stand-in GitHub. It covers the reply link on the admin page, the owner's POST, the reader's message and the reply showing after the feedback box, and another reader and a visitor seeing neither.

**Mutations.** I made seven of my own, through `-overlay` so the tree was never touched. They differ from the build's and the code review's, and the tests caught every one:
- SenderThreads ignoring which report it is reading;
- OwnerReply ignoring a write that inserted nothing;
- the reader's own thread drawn above the form;
- the reply body read with FormValue;
- OwnerReply skipping Normalize;
- a SenderThreads read error swallowed instead of making the page a 503;
- the 303 losing its #feedback-n fragment.

**Real headless Chrome** (CHROME_BIN), on the running binary, with the signed-in session passed through a small scratch proxy:
- Reader A's report page shows the form, then "You wrote" with their message, then the reply with its Author badge underneath.
- Reader B sees only their own message.
- Reader A, on the other report, sees only the message they sent there.
- The admin page shows a "Send reply" form with an aria-label on each message, and the reply drawn under the message it answers.
- At 1000 px and 500 px wide the layout is clean.
- No probe Chrome process was left running, and the probe profiles were deleted.

**Process.** No loop: every stage has a single attempt. The critique and critique review each passed in under a second with no account, as the code review already noted.

**Not reached:** real GitHub OAuth, the VPS and WireGuard proxy, real https, phone browsers at 390 px, the light colour scheme on signed-in pages, and production data.

checks.evidence: All 11 packages ok, including internal/server (12.2 s), internal/feedback and internal/fitnessrules. testutil/fakegithub has no test files. Exit 0.

checks.command: python -I .taad-scratch/validate1/readfinish.py (sqlite3 file:C:/Users/sshub/AppData/Roaming/taad3/engine.db?mode=ro, SELECT id, finish FROM epics WHERE id=43, closed), then python -I .taad-scratch/validate1/tests/acceptance/test_e005_1_private_feedback.py with ROOT patched to the worktree
checks.evidence: Ran 1 test in 4.526s, OK, exit 0. The ledger row says needs_its_test: true, path tests/acceptance/test_e005_1_private_feedback.py, body of 21624 chars. The reply assertions at body lines 351-361 all held.
29 rules checked against 68 parsed files: every declared rule holds.

checks.what: Mutant M2: senderSQL ignores report_id (case h)
checks.evidence: Killed, exit 1. Failing: TestFeedbackDoesNotInterfere (reader thread subtest), TestFeedbackFollowsReportLifecycle, TestFeedbackSenderSeesOnlyTheirOwnThread, TestSenderThreads.

checks.what: Mutant M4: OwnerReply returns nil when the INSERT…SELECT inserts 0 rows (case c race)
Mutant M5: own-feedback <ol> moved above the feedback form (cases a, i)
checks.command: same go test with overlay on feedback.html
checks.evidence: Killed, exit 1. Failing: TestFeedbackReply, TestFeedbackReplyMarkup, TestFeedbackReplyToUnpublishedReport, TestFeedbackSenderSeesOnlyTheirOwnThread, TestFeedbackDoesNotInterfere, TestFeedbackSend, TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout.

checks.what: Mutant M6: reply body read with r.FormValue, so the query string counts and repeats pass (case d, exactly one body)
checks.command: same go test with overlay on admin.go

checks.what: Mutant M7: OwnerReply skips comments.Normalize (case d)
checks.command: same go test with overlay on feedback.go
checks.evidence: Killed, exit 1. Failing: TestFeedbackReplyBodies, TestFeedbackReplyTargets, TestFeedbackStoreFailure/the_reply_write_fails, TestOwnerReplyRefusedBodyRunsNoSQL, TestOwnerReplyStoresAndNormalises.

checks.what: Mutant M8: a SenderThreads read error is logged but the page stays found (case j)
checks.command: same go test with overlay on reader.go

checks.what: Mutant M9: reply 303 without the #feedback-<n> fragment (case a)
checks.command: same go test with overlay on admin.go
checks.evidence: Killed, exit 1. Failing: TestFeedbackReply, ReplyBodies, ReplyTargets, ReplyMarkup, ReplyToUnpublishedReport, SenderSeesOnlyTheirOwnThread, FollowsReportLifecycle, DoesNotInterfere, StoreFailure and TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout. The tree was left unchanged: git status showed no src changes.

checks.what: The case (b) id table includes x, 0, -1, +1 and 01
checks.evidence: feedback_test.go:1195 tries x, 0, -1, +1, 01, 001, 1x, x1, 1.0, %201, 1%20, 2^64-sized and int64-overflow ids, 99, 3 and an Arabic-Indic digit.

checks.what: Handler order matches the design: canonicalID → OwnerReplyTarget → MaxBytesReader(maxCommentBody) with exactly one PostForm body → OwnerReply → 303 to /admin/reports/<slug>#feedback-<n>
checks.evidence: admin.go:43 adds the adminRoutes row and admin.go:163-206 follows the designed order. replySQL (feedback.go:291) is a single INSERT…SELECT with no transaction. SenderThreads filters on both report_id and github_id and returns nil without a query when the id is 0 or less. renderReader (reader.go:139-153) calls it only when stateFound && signedIn && !v.IsOwner, and a read error makes the page stateUnavailable.

checks.what: Real headless Chrome on the built binary: the signed-in reader's own thread and the owner's admin reply form
checks.command: python -I .taad-scratch/validate1/tests/acceptance/probe_e005_shots.py (a scratch copy of the finish test that saves each page's HTML and screenshots it through CHROME_BIN via a cookie-injecting loopback proxy; the last run hides only .report-frame)
checks.evidence: Every run exited 0 with the test OK. In shots4/reader-s1-noframe.png reader A sees the form, then 'You wrote' with their message, then the 'Author' badge and the reply. In reader-s2-noframe-narrow.png (500 px) reader B sees only their own message, with no reply. reader-s1-other.html (A on the beta report) has one own-feedback item and no alpha text. owner-admin-wide.png shows a 'Send reply' textarea and button per message (aria-label 'Reply to @login') with the reply under reader A's message. No reader HTML contains feedback-<digit> or /admin/feedback/.

The capture is a crop of a wider layout: the header and the note are cut at the right edge, and the iframe's right border is off-screen. Headless Chrome's window does not honour a width this narrow, so this measures the tool, not the page. The engine's own 390 px screen of the signed-out page lays out correctly, and at 500 px the signed-in page wraps cleanly.
It captured an almost blank, unpainted frame, about 6 KB. I replaced it with the frame-hidden capture above, which did draw.

checks.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='chrome.exe'" | Where CommandLine -like '*validate1*'; Remove-Item of the 23 tmp* user-data dirs under .taad-scratch/validate1

criteria.criterion: PS-017: from the admin feedback view the author writes a reply to a feedback message, and it stays private between the author and that reader
criteria.how: The finish test, run from a scratch copy, exits 0: the owner posts through /admin/feedback/<n>/reply from the admin view, and another reader and a visitor see neither the message nor the reply. Real Chrome on the binary showed the same. TestFeedbackDoesNotInterfere's per-label noninterference subtest passes, and the M2 and M5 mutants broke it.

criteria.criterion: SC-018 (merged): the reader sees their own feedback and the author's replies beneath the feedback box
criteria.how: reader-s1.html has <ol class="own-feedback"> after the form and the hidden #feedback-sent note, holding the message and the reply. The real-Chrome screenshot shows it drawn under the box. The finish test asserts the box comes before the message and the reply.

criteria.criterion: (a) Owner replies with a valid body: 303 to #feedback-<n>, one feedback_replies row, the reply under its message on the admin page, and the sender sees the message and the reply after the form's action text
criteria.how: TestFeedbackReply passes, and the M9 mutant (fragment dropped) and the M5 mutant (thread drawn above the form) both kill it. The admin screenshot shows the reply under its message.

criteria.criterion: (b) n is 'x', '0', '-1', '+1' or '01': 404 and nothing written; the TestAdminAccessMatrix row stays green
criteria.how: TestFeedbackReplyTargets' id table at feedback_test.go:1195 includes them all, and it and TestAdminAccessMatrix pass in the full suite.

criteria.criterion: (c) An unknown n, or a message deleted with its report: 404 and nothing written
criteria.how: TestFeedbackReplyTargets passes, and the M4 mutant (0 rows treated as success) kills it and TestOwnerReplyNeedsAMessage.

criteria.criterion: (d) Reply bodies follow the same refused and accepted table as TestFeedbackBodies: 400, or stored normalised
criteria.how: TestFeedbackReplyBodies passes. The M6 mutant (FormValue) and the M7 mutant (no Normalize) both kill it.

criteria.criterion: (e) A reply to a draft report's feedback is stored, and the reader sees it only once the report is published
criteria.how: TestFeedbackReplyToUnpublishedReport passes in the suite, and the M5 mutant also turns it red, so it reads the drawn thread.

criteria.criterion: (f) Non-owner and anonymous POSTs get 403, through the access matrix
criteria.how: TestFeedbackReplyIsTheOwnersAlone and TestAdminAccessMatrix pass. The route is an adminRoutes row (admin.go:43), behind the owner gate.

criteria.criterion: (g) Per-label noninterference: B's message and its reply change no observe() observation and none of A's pages; B sees exactly B's thread
criteria.how: The TestFeedbackDoesNotInterfere subtest 'a reader's thread and the author's reply to it reach nobody else' passes. The M2 and M5 mutants kill it.

criteria.criterion: (h) The sender sees only their own messages on that report: not their message on another report, not another reader's
criteria.how: TestFeedbackSenderSeesOnlyTheirOwnThread passes, and the M2 mutant kills it. In the probe, reader A's beta page showed only the beta message, and reader B's alpha page only B's message.

criteria.criterion: (i) TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout, seeded with feedback and a reply, keeps / and /reports/newest identical for that sender
criteria.how: It passes in the suite, and the M5 mutant kills it.

criteria.criterion: (j) A SenderThreads read failure makes the reader page 503; a reply write failure gives 500
criteria.how: TestFeedbackStoreFailure's subtests 'the sender's thread read fails' and 'the reply write fails' pass. The M8 mutant (error swallowed) kills the 503 subtest.

criteria.criterion: (k) No reader page contains 'feedback-' followed by a digit, or '/admin/feedback/'
criteria.how: The feedbackIDRE checks in the tests pass. None of the probe's real reader HTML (reader-s1, reader-s2, reader-s1-other) contains either: the only feedback- ids are feedback-sent, feedback-message and feedback-reply.

criteria.criterion: (l) TestFeedbackFollowsReportLifecycle repeated with replies written through OwnerReply
criteria.how: It passes. The M2 and M9 mutants both make it fail, which shows it exercises the reply route and the sender thread.

The ledger's exact body exits 0 against this tree. The one change is ROOT, set to the worktree path, which is what its dirname×3 would compute at tests/acceptance. The file itself is engine-planted (needs_its_test: true) and is not in the repo, so the literal command from the repo root cannot run until the engine places it.

obligations.evidence: Each case named in O-001's discharge text exists and passes in `go test -count=1 ./...`. Seven independent overlay mutants were all killed by those tests, and the E-005 finish test exits 0 from a scratch copy of the ledger body with ROOT patched.

problems.what: It is the signed-out report page, so it shows none of what SL-009 added: the reader's own thread and the admin reply form are drawn only when signed in. I looked at those separately in my own headless-Chrome captures.

The frame is an empty white box, the visible result of the frame-ancestors console error the engine already listed. It comes from the harness origin (127.0.0.1 vs https://hband.test), not from this slice.
The very long unbroken login wraps onto its own lines below the avatar, so the avatar sits alone on a line and the date drops to a third line. This is the SL-008 thread layout, not SL-009.
Each avatar shows as a broken-image icon, which matches the img-src CSP errors already listed. The fixture's avatars.example host is the cause, not this slice.
Signed out, so the SL-009 surfaces are not on it.

not_reached: Real GitHub OAuth sign-in. Every signed-in path ran against the stand-in GitHub from the finish test harness.
The VPS reverse proxy over WireGuard and real https. Requests came from loopback with X-Forwarded-Proto/For headers set by the harness.
How the signed-in pages render at 390 px on a real phone, and in Firefox or Safari. My 390 px headless capture was a crop of a wider layout; only 500 px and wider were seen properly.
The signed-in pages in the light colour scheme. My Chrome captures came out dark.
The signed-in pages with their real CSP headers in a browser. The probe proxy passed only Content-Type, and the last capture hid the report frame on purpose.
The finish test run as its literal command from the repo root. tests/acceptance/test_e005_1_private_feedback.py is not in the tree, and only a scratch copy with ROOT patched was run.
Page size and load time of the owner's admin page with many messages (Q-023, still open). There is now one form per message; this was not measured.
Production database state. No migration was added; 0005 already had feedback_replies, but prod user_version was not checked (Q-015/Q-016).
